inputs.text: After years of a system that left ordinary Cubans with little property and too little money to buy the businesses still functioning, a political transition could leave them shut out once again. Wealthy members of the diaspora—and possibly foreign investors—may be positioned to buy up property at bargain prices while Cuban residents watch their own country pass into other hands. A real transition should put Cuban families and local ownership first, not turn the island into a clearance sale for those with money.
